input: Find bribery and market-manipulation enforcement actions involving Glencore since 2018

events.summary: Dutch authorities opened an investigation into suspected bribery to obtain copper and cobalt mining licences; the case against this entity was dismissed on 5 August 2024 following the Swiss resolution, while co-defendant investigations continued at that announcement.
events.jurisdiction: Netherlands; conduct in Democratic Republic of the Congo

events.type: Commodity-market enforcement: position limits, wash trades and reporting
events.amount: US$2 million civil monetary penalty, jointly and severally (as_of: 2018-04-30).
events.parties: Glencore Agriculture B.V. (formerly Glencore Grain B.V.); Glencore Ltd.
events.summary: The CFTC settled charges over cotton-futures position-limit breaches, illegal exchange-for-physical wash trades and inaccurate reports; this was separate from the later oil-benchmark manipulation case.

events.parties: Glencore Ltd., subsidiary of Glencore plc
events.summary: A subpoena dated 2 July and disclosed on 3 July sought FCPA and money-laundering compliance records concerning group business in Nigeria, DRC and Venezuela.
Glencore disclosed that the CFTC was investigating possible Commodity Exchange Act and regulatory violations through corrupt commodity practices, with a scope similar to the DOJ investigation.

events.parties: Glencore UK Ltd.; Glencore Energy (UK) Ltd.
events.summary: The SFO opened its oil-trading corruption investigation, which subsequently produced the corporate bribery prosecution.

events.parties: Emilio Jose Heredia Collado, former Glencore Ltd. senior fuel-oil trader
events.summary: Heredia pleaded guilty to conspiring to manipulate the Platts Los Angeles 380 CST Bunker Fuel assessment; the opened DOJ release does not establish his eventual sentence.

events.type: Foreign-bribery and money-laundering conspiracies — related individual
events.summary: Stimler pleaded guilty to FCPA and money-laundering conspiracies involving payments to Nigerian officials for favourable oil contracts.

events.amount: US$428,521,173 criminal fine and US$272,185,792 forfeiture/disgorgement; nearly US$256 million in potential credits for related resolutions (as_of: 2022-05-24).
events.summary: The company pleaded guilty to conspiracy to violate the FCPA over a decade-long multinational bribery scheme and agreed to an independent compliance monitor.
events.jurisdiction: United States — DOJ; Southern District of New York

events.amount: US$341,221,682 criminal fine and US$144,417,203 forfeiture, with over US$242 million credited for CFTC payments (as_of: 2022-05-24).
events.summary: Glencore Ltd. pleaded guilty to conspiring to manipulate fuel-oil prices at US ports and agreed to an independent compliance monitor.
events.jurisdiction: United States — DOJ; District of Connecticut

events.amount: US$865,630,784 civil monetary penalty and US$320,715,066 disgorgement; offsets apply for overlapping resolutions (as_of: 2022-05-24).
events.parties: Glencore International A.G.; Glencore Ltd.; Chemoil Corporation
events.summary: The CFTC settled charges involving manipulation or attempted manipulation of oil benchmarks and related derivatives, false reporting and corrupt practices.

events.amount: Approximately US$39.6 million, including US$29.6 million reimbursement/reversal of undue advantages, US$9.8 million improbity fine and US$145,900 anti-corruption fine (as_of: 2022-06-09).
events.parties: Glencore; the opened Brazilian-resolution account does not specify the exact contracting legal entity
events.summary: Glencore signed an MPF leniency agreement concerning bribes to Petrobras employees for favourable fuel transactions and committed to improve compliance.

events.amount: Over US$25 million in bribes alleged (as_of: 2022-05-24); this is conduct value, not a penalty.
events.summary: The SFO charged five substantive bribery offences and two failures to prevent bribery concerning oil operations in Cameroon, Equatorial Guinea, Ivory Coast, Nigeria and South Sudan.
The company pleaded guilty to all seven Bribery Act counts; an amended count was pleaded to again on 31 October before sentencing.

events.amount: US$341.2 million fine and US$144.4 million forfeiture, reported in rounded terms (as_of: 2022-09-23).
events.summary: A federal judge imposed the oil-price-manipulation sentence under the May plea agreement; this is a later milestone in the same criminal case, not an additional penalty.

events.amount: GBP182,935,392 fine; GBP93,479,338.95 confiscation; GBP4,550,362 prosecution costs (as_of: 2022-11-03).
events.summary: The court sentenced the corporate defendant for its oil-trading bribery offences and expressly made no culpability finding against any particular individual.

events.parties: Glencore International AG, on behalf of its Congolese-associated companies
events.summary: The agreement covered present and future DRC claims arising from alleged group corruption during 2007–2018, with admissions limited to conduct already acknowledged in the DOJ resolution.

events.amount: Approximately US$700 million: US$428.5 million fine and US$272 million forfeiture, as reported (as_of: 2023-02-28).
events.summary: The court imposed the sentence contemplated by the earlier FCPA plea agreement; this is not an additional resolution to be added to the plea amounts.
events.jurisdiction: United States — Southern District of New York

events.amount: Approximately CHF27 million compensation claim, also described as US$29 million (as_of: 2024-08-05, reporting the May 2023 order).
events.summary: The OAG partially abandoned proceedings concerning two facts linked to the US guilty plea while ordering compensation.
events.jurisdiction: Switzerland — Office of the Attorney General

events.type: Failure to prevent foreign bribery — summary penalty order
events.amount: CHF2 million fine and US$150 million compensation claim (as_of: 2024-08-05).
events.summary: The final order found organisational failures concerning a business partner’s bribery in a mining-stake acquisition, while other DRC allegations were abandoned; Glencore waived appeal.
events.jurisdiction: Switzerland — Office of the Attorney General; conduct in DRC

events.type: Bribery conspiracy and document-falsification charges — related individuals
events.parties: Alex Beard; Andrew Gibson; Paul Hopkirk; Ramon Labiaga; Martin Wakefield; David Perez
events.summary: Five former employees were charged in August and Perez in September; the latest opened SFO case page records an open case, four not-guilty pleas on 10 November 2025 and trial listed for 4 October 2027.
Glencore reports that the DOJ ended its monitorships early in March 2025 and that the plea-agreement term concluded in 2026; these are resolution-status updates, not new offences.

output.assessment: As of 2026-11-10, the record indicates substantial historical bribery and commodity-market misconduct risk, with corporate convictions and settlements across several jurisdictions; liabilities belong to the named legal defendants and must not automatically be attributed to Glencore plc, and overlapping US penalties and later sentencing milestones must not be added together. The company reports early termination of its DOJ monitorships and completion of the plea-agreement term, but related UK individual proceedings remain open, with trial listed for 4 October 2027. No unrelated namesake was identified; Fleurette Properties Ltd is a separate counterparty-related defendant rather than a Glencore penalty, and the precise Brazilian contracting entity and final US individual sentences remain unverified.
